To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the residual information of the original image can be exploited to identify the original image among a few templates, and that such residual information can be hidden in the compression artifacts.
the compression artifacts can be used to identify redacted images among a small set of templates.

(a) when the redaction replaces pixels in the compressed images, the redacted images contain residual information of the original images, and (b) this residual information can be exploited to identify the original images when the images are compressed in higher bit rates than the original images.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the security of images that are redacted before dissemination and compressed for efficient transmission.
the residual information in redacted images, and its potential impact on the security and privacy of sensitive information.
the following question: How much information can be extracted from the redacted images?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
redacted images should be compressed at the same or lower bit-rate than the original images, in order to minimize the residual information.
the residual information of the original image is hidden in the compression artifacts and the adversary can exploit the residual information to identify the original image.
, if the image is compressed at higher bit rate than the original, and the entropy of the original is low, the redacted image can be used to identify the original image.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the redaction of images is not a trivial problem and the security of redacted images must be carefully considered.
redacting images with black and white is not as safe as one might expect.
, when an image is compressed in a lossy way, it is not enough to replace all the pixels of a region of interest with black or white.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in general, it is not safe to redact sensitive information in a lossy compressed image without considering its compression artifacts.
, when the image is redacted, the residual information of the original image can be exploited by the adversary.
the compression of the redacted image must be done in a way that is different from the compression of the template images.
